en: Title: *Puṣpakūṭa-nāma-dhāraṇī* Source: Testimonia from various sources

"Siṃhavikrīḍita, whoever shall perform worship to the Tathāgata—whether he is present or has passed into parinirvāṇa—all of them shall attain parinirvāṇa by means of one of the three vehicles. Furthermore, Siṃhavikrīḍita, if someone, upon seeing the Tathāgata, Arhat, Samyaksaṃbuddha, should develop a serene mind, and with a serene mind should honor, revere, respect, worship, and serve him; and should attend upon him with gains, robes, alms-food, bedding and seats, and medicinal requisites for the sick, as well as all articles of comfort; and if another should perform worship to the body of the Tathāgata who has passed into parinirvāṇa within a relic the size of a mustard seed—the maturation of the fruit is to be expected as equal. Thus, regarding such worship, there is no distinction or difference whatsoever."

Furthermore, Siṃhavikrīḍita, suppose someone were to attend upon the Tathāgata face-to-face for a year, or a thousand years, or a hundred thousand years, providing him with every article of comfort; and suppose another person, having embraced the thought of awakening (bodhicitta), were to place a single flower upon a shrine of the Tathāgata who has passed into parinirvāṇa for the sake of worshipping the Tathāgata, or offer a handful of water, or sprinkle water, or lay down a blade of grass, or remove the faded flowers, or perform an offering of ointment, or an offering of flowers, or an offering of lamps—doing so with a joyful mind, or even after taking a single step forward, uttering the words: "Homage to that Buddha, the Blessed One. Regarding this, Siṃhavikrīḍita, you should have no doubt, uncertainty, or hesitation that such a person would fall into the miserable states or the abyss for an eon, or a hundred eons, or a thousand eons; such a thing is impossible.
